speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe when you first noticed the rash on your scalp and forehead, and have you tried any treatments for it so far?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash cause significant itching or discomfort for the infant, and do you observe any similar red, scaly patches in the diaper area or skin folds?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the greasy yellow scales and distribution, this presentation is highly suggestive of seborrheic dermatitis rather than psoriasis. I will proceed to confirm the diagnosis based on these classic clinical features.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Seborrheic dermatitis
